questions.prompt: Does an antecedent necessarily cause the following behaviour?
questions.answer: No; temporal order alone does not establish causation.

questions.prompt: Why consider commercial and structural influences?
questions.answer: Access, promotion and social conditions may shape behaviour and harm beyond individual choices.
questions.feedback: Avoid attributing all responsibility to willpower.

questions.prompt: May learners deliberately provoke a clinical trigger to investigate it?
questions.answer: No; this lesson uses fictional observations only.
questions.feedback: Clinical exposure belongs with qualified care.

questions.prompt: What is a proportionate environmental option?
questions.answer: A voluntary, low-risk adjustment or support request consistent with the person's wishes.
questions.feedback: Do not impose surveillance or restrictions.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer, formative only; use specific feedback and delayed retest.
scoring.practice: Maps contextual influences, distinguishes hypotheses from causes and proposes voluntary support without inducing distress.
scoring.transfer: Produce a context map for a novel fictional case. Include an environmental influence, an unknown internal experience, two rival explanations and a consent-based support option. Explain why the map cannot determine a clinical intervention.
scoring.pass: All mapped criteria require Level 2 evidence; never average away missing or safety-critical evidence. Quizzes cannot certify competence.
